## Simple explanation

GELU, or Gaussian Error Linear Unit, is a smooth activation function
commonly used in Transformer models. Unlike ReLU, it does not abruptly
set every negative input to zero.

## Technical explanation

The exact GELU function is $x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi$ is the standard
normal cumulative distribution function. A common approximation is
$0.5x\left(1+\tanh\left(\sqrt{2/\pi}(x+0.044715x^3)\right)\right)$.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Activation functions affect optimization and model behaviour. GELU is
widely associated with Transformer architectures, and implementations
may use an approximation for computational efficiency.

## How it works

GELU scales an input according to the probability that a standard
normally distributed variable is less than that input. This creates a
smooth nonlinear transformation that retains small negative values
rather than applying a hard cutoff.

## Practical example

A Transformer feedforward block may apply GELU between two learned
linear transformations before passing activations onward.

## Common misconceptions

- GELU is not simply ReLU with a different name.
- Different libraries may expose exact and approximate implementations.
- Choosing GELU does not by itself guarantee better model performance.
